statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-43871 (the TCompactProtocol varint reader has no byte-count limit, which can cause an infinite loop) affects Apache Thrift before 0.24.0, including the Go library github.com/apache/thrift: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8wv5-x4w7-5gww. The fix is https://github.com/apache/thrift/commit/d5152211af61f850ec393604316804096dd4632e (Add byte-count limit to TCompactProtocol varint reader), which changes lib/go/thrift/compact_protocol.go and was released in 0.24.0. Read the Go build information (go version -m) of /usr/bin/jaeger, the only file in the package, in every published build of the jaeger-dev package for Alpine 3.24 in the DHI Alpine repository, on both x86_64 and aarch64: 21 builds, 2.19.0-r1 through 2.23.0-r4. Each is a statically linked Go program built with CGO_ENABLED=0 for GOOS=linux. github.com/apache/thrift is the pseudo-version v0.23.1-0.20260429145742-d2acd3c49e58 in 2.19.0-r1 to 2.20.0-r3, v0.24.0 in 2.20.0-r4 to 2.22.0-r3, and v0.25.0 from 2.23.0-r0. That pseudo-version is commit d2acd3c49e58 of 2026-04-29, a descendant of the fix commit (https://github.com/apache/thrift/compare/d5152211af61...d2acd3c49e58), so it already contains the fix even though it sorts below 0.24.0. The vulnerable function is linked in every build: the Go function table (pclntab) of /usr/bin/jaeger lists github.com/apache/thrift/lib/go/thrift.(*TCompactProtocol).readVarint64, the varint reader the fix changes, in all 42 builds checked here (21 versions on two architectures), with runtime.main found in the same table as a control, so the decision rests on the thrift version and not on absence. Every published build carries the fix, so the fixed version is the first published build, 2.19.0-r1.

CVE-2026-43871 (GHSA-8wv5-x4w7-5gww): before 0.24.0, the TCompactProtocol varint reader of the Apache Thrift Go library (and the Python, PHP and Java bindings) has no byte-count limit, so crafted input can make it loop without end. It is fixed in 0.24.0 by the upstream commit that caps varint reads at 10 bytes: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8wv5-x4w7-5gww, https://lists.apache.org/thread/7v3jhgwfbmhx42424phydlnzb109g8b9, https://github.com/apache/thrift/commit/d5152211af61. /usr/bin/alloy contains the Thrift compact protocol reader in every build. Read the Go build information of /usr/bin/alloy in every published alloy-dev package for Debian 13 in the DHI Debian repository, 1.18.1-0 to 1.22.0-16, on amd64 and arm64 (1.21.2-0 was published for arm64 only); 87 packages, with no debug-symbol packages published for this source. The github.com/apache/thrift version by build is 1.18.1-0 to 1.18.1-3: 0.23.1-0.20260429145742-d2acd3c49e58; 1.19.0-0 to 1.21.3-5: 0.24.0; 1.22.0-0 to 1.22.0-16: 0.25.0. The pseudo-version v0.23.1-0.20260429145742-d2acd3c49e58 is upstream commit d2acd3c49e58 of 2026-04-29, which descends from the fix commit d5152211af61 of 2026-04-23 (https://github.com/apache/thrift/compare/d5152211af61...d2acd3c49e58), so every published build carries the fix even though that pseudo-version sorts below 0.24.0. The range therefore ends at 1.18.1-0, the lowest published build. The error message the fix adds to the Go library ("variable-length int over 10 bytes") is present in /usr/bin/alloy in every build, including 1.18.1-0 to 1.18.1-3.
